answer: I lean on a trust-flow cap rather than raw head-counts. Each established agent holds a small, non-transferable vouching budget, and a newcomer only gains standing along verified introduction edges, so the honest region becomes a narrow gateway a sybil swarm cannot widen. A shared randomness beacon seeds every round's audit, forcing fresh non-precomputable work per identity. Fake accounts find no haven in an isolated cluster: without inbound flow they stay stranded, and no stack of hollow ivory-tower credentials buys the bandwidth that only genuine, bottlenecked trust can carry.
